title: CloudFormation Resources and Dependencies
learning_outcomes: Explain the purpose of cloudformation resources and dependencies and its relationship to Infrastructure as Code (IaC).
Interpret the example and identify at least one prerequisite or boundary relevant to cloudformation resources and dependencies.
Propose a safe verification or troubleshooting step and record one security, reliability or cost consideration.

content.intro: In this lesson, you will learn cloudformation resources and dependencies in the context of Infrastructure as Code (IaC). You will connect the listed subtopics to a practical decision, inspect a small example, and define evidence that would confirm or disprove your assumptions.
content.why_it_matters: CloudFormation Resources and Dependencies matters because it is one part of infrastructure as code. Real workloads depend on explicit prerequisites, correct permissions, predictable behavior and a way to verify outcomes. Learning the decision points helps you distinguish a working demonstration from a safe and supportable design.

content_blocks.title: Module 16: Infrastructure as Code (IaC)
content_blocks.alt_text: Five-step overview for module 16, Infrastructure as Code (IaC), followed by verification, least-privilege security, recovery, and cost-cleanup checks.
content_blocks.caption: Module 16 learning sequence: understand the concept, make a controlled design/configuration, verify behavior, and document security/reliability/cost trade-offs.

content_blocks.title: Core idea
content_blocks.text:
**Core idea.** CloudFormation Resources and Dependencies belongs to Infrastructure as Code (IaC). Infrastructure as code makes configuration reviewable and reproducible. Treat plans/change sets as review artifacts, separate state/secrets, detect drift, and test failure/rollback paths.

The PDF lists these subtopics: Resource declarations; References and attribute retrieval; Dependency ordering; Resource replacement behavior. Treat them as a connected workflow rather than a list to memorize. Start with the workload requirement, identify the AWS resource/control involved, and write down who owns configuration and operation.

content_blocks.title: Practical reasoning
content_blocks.text: **Apply it safely.** For cloudformation resources and dependencies, name the prerequisites and the expected result before making a change. Prefer a read-only inspection or local/static example first. Then plan a normal case, a failure case, and a verification step. In a live account, require the account owner-approved sandbox, narrow permissions, spend visibility and cleanup plan. Do not put credentials in code or commit local configuration files.

items.title: Resource declarations
items.text: Identify the AWS resource or design decision involved, the permissions and prerequisites it needs, and the evidence that shows it is configured as intended.

items.title: References and attribute retrieval
items.text: Define the input/data permissions, expected evidence, evaluation cases, safety boundaries and cost limits. A generated answer or completed invocation is not by itself proof of correctness.

items.title: Dependency ordering
items.text: Write a verification step and a failure case. For hands-on work, start with read-only inspection and use an approved sandbox before changing cloud resources.

items.title: Resource replacement behavior
items.text: Record ownership, dependencies and teardown/recovery behavior so the design can be operated safely after the first successful test.

content_blocks.title: CloudFormation secure S3 resource excerpt: CloudFormation Resources and Dependencies
content_blocks.code:
Resources:
  PrivateAssetsBucket:
    Type: AWS::S3::Bucket
    Properties:
      PublicAccessBlockConfiguration:
        BlockPublicAcls: true
        IgnorePublicAcls: true
        BlockPublicPolicy: true
        RestrictPublicBuckets: true
      VersioningConfiguration:
        Status: Enabled
content_blocks.expected_output: A template excerpt defining an S3 bucket with public access blocked and versioning enabled; review full-stack policies and cost before deployment.
content_blocks.run_instructions: This block is an inspectable example, not an AWS action performed by CodeLeaf. Review the example as text and adapt it only after checking current official service documentation. Do not apply/deploy changes in a real account without account-owner approval, least-privilege permissions and a reviewed cost/cleanup plan.
content_blocks.reset_steps: No AWS resource is created by this lesson example. If you independently run an approved lab, capture the starting state first, follow the lab-specific teardown instructions, check dependent resources and billing/resource inventories, and document anything retained.
content_blocks.limitations: The CodeLeaf playground is an HTML/CSS/JavaScript preview and does not execute AWS APIs, shell commands, SQL or cloud deployments. Treat output as illustrative; live values depend on credentials, permissions, Region, service state and schema.

content_blocks.title: Security and cost checkpoint
content_blocks.text: Use least privilege, keep Block Public Access/private defaults unless a justified reviewed requirement says otherwise, and document cost/cleanup before live changes.

task: Create a one-page decision card for “CloudFormation Resources and Dependencies”. State the goal, prerequisites, the AWS resource or control involved, the expected result, one read-only/static verification step, one failure case, the relevant permission boundary, and cost/cleanup considerations. Do not create or alter billable resources unless the account owner has approved the lab.
hints: Start from the exact subtopics in the lesson and define the desired state in your own words.
Prefer a read-only check or static artifact before a mutating command; record the identity/Region and required permissions.
Verify the expected result and a failure path using current official documentation; write down cost and cleanup implications.
expected_output: A short reviewable decision card for CloudFormation Resources and Dependencies with prerequisites, evidence, a failure case, security implications and cost/cleanup notes.

common_mistakes.problem: Treating one successful example as proof of production readiness.
common_mistakes.why: The example may not test permissions, regional/service prerequisites, retries, recovery, quotas or edge cases.
common_mistakes.fix: Write acceptance criteria, test a failure path, inspect logs/state and record the limits of the result.

common_mistakes.problem: Changing a live resource before confirming its effect and cost.
common_mistakes.why: Cloud changes can expose data, break traffic or leave billable dependencies behind.
common_mistakes.fix: Start read-only, use an approved sandbox, review the change, tag ownership and verify cleanup.

common_mistakes.problem: Copying broad permissions or credentials into source files.
common_mistakes.why: Broad permissions and leaked long-lived credentials increase the impact of mistakes.
common_mistakes.fix: Use scoped roles/temporary credentials, keep secrets in approved stores and review access boundaries.

summary: CloudFormation Resources and Dependencies is taught as part of Infrastructure as Code (IaC).
Infrastructure as code makes configuration reviewable and reproducible. Treat plans/change sets as review artifacts, separate state/secrets, detect drift, and test failure/rollback paths.
Verify assumptions with official service documentation and evidence from the relevant AWS resource, logs or tests.
For live labs, confirm permissions and likely charges before acting, then verify cleanup.
